founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-bara: Ratify 'create' / 'Creator' for all 14 Isaiah sites (overlay bara-create-isaiah). Yes, the Genesis 'shape' should be reviewed at the next Genesis pass. Reasons: (1) the Qal/Niphal never takes an accusative of material and the lexica gloss it 'create' (BDB; HALOT brʾ I; Bernhardt TDOT 2; Schmidt THAT 1). (2) The central bara rationale's 'Piel "cut out, fashion"' is the separate homonym 'cut down, clear (forest)' (Josh 17:15, 18; Ezek 23:47; HALOT). Its '(Gesenius §17)' locator is wrong as a GKC reference, since GKC §17 treats Qere/Ketiv. (3) The central yatsar entry glosses yāṣar 'form, shape, fashion (as a potter)', so 'shape' for bārāʾ already collides with the potter's verb even in Genesis. (4) The canon itself uses 'créés, formés et faits' (Isa 43:7). Corpus finding: AMO-WOH-4:13 already renders bôrēʾ rûaḥ 'shapes the wind', an extension of the Genesis 'shape' outside the central appliesTo that is now inconsistent with Isaiah. Review it together with the Genesis decision. Options for the Genesis review: re-render 'create' and keep the bārāʾ/ʿāśāh/yāṣar distinction as create/make/form (the Isaiah model), or keep 'shape' but downgrade the central entry to speculative with a corrected rationale.

paragraphs.text: רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה פִּצְחִ֨י רִנָּ֤ה וְצַהֲלִי֙ לֹא־חָ֔לָה כִּֽי־רַבִּ֧ים בְּֽנֵי־שׁוֹמֵמָ֛ה מִבְּנֵ֥י בְעוּלָ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: Sing, O barren one, who did not bear; break forth into singing and cry aloud, you who did not travail! For the children of the desolate one are more than the children of the married one, says YHWH.
i18n.he: רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה פִּצְחִ֨י רִנָּ֤ה וְצַהֲלִי֙ לֹא־חָ֔לָה כִּֽי־רַבִּ֧ים בְּֽנֵי־שׁוֹמֵמָ֛ה מִבְּנֵ֥י בְעוּלָ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

notes.official: *ronnî ʿăqārāh* “Sing, O barren one.” Zion is addressed as a barren woman who will have more children than the married one. The image draws on the barren matriarchs (Sarah, Rachel, Hannah), and Gal 4:27 quotes the verse.

paragraphs.text: הַרְחִ֣יבִי ׀ מְק֣וֹם אָהֳלֵ֗ךְ וִירִיע֧וֹת מִשְׁכְּנוֹתַ֛יִךְ יַטּ֖וּ אַל־תַּחְשֹׂ֑כִי הַאֲרִ֙יכִי֙ מֵֽיתָרַ֔יִךְ וִיתֵדֹתַ֖יִךְ חַזֵּֽקִי׃

i18n.en: Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch out the curtains of your dwellings; do not hold back; lengthen your cords and strengthen your stakes.
i18n.he: הַרְחִ֣יבִי ׀ מְק֣וֹם אָהֳלֵ֗ךְ וִירִיע֧וֹת מִשְׁכְּנוֹתַ֛יִךְ יַטּ֖וּ אַל־תַּחְשֹׂ֑כִי הַאֲרִ֙יכִי֙ מֵֽיתָרַ֔יִךְ וִיתֵדֹתַ֖יִךְ חַזֵּֽקִי׃

paragraphs.text: כִּי־יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹ֖אול תִּפְרֹ֑צִי וְזַרְעֵךְ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם יִירָ֔שׁ וְעָרִ֥ים נְשַׁמּ֖וֹת יוֹשִֽׁיבוּ׃

i18n.en: For you will spread out to the right and to the left, and your seed will possess the nations, and they will people the desolate cities.
i18n.he: כִּי־יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹ֖אול תִּפְרֹ֑צִי וְזַרְעֵךְ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם יִירָ֔שׁ וְעָרִ֥ים נְשַׁמּ֖וֹת יוֹשִֽׁיבוּ׃

paragraphs.text: אַל־תִּֽירְאִי֙ כִּי־לֹ֣א תֵב֔וֹשִׁי וְאַל־תִּכָּלְמִ֖י כִּ֣י לֹ֣א תַחְפִּ֑ירִי כִּ֣י בֹ֤שֶׁת עֲלוּמַ֙יִךְ֙ תִּשְׁכָּ֔חִי וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת אַלְמְנוּתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֥א תִזְכְּרִי־עֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: Do not fear, for you will not be ashamed; do not be confounded, for you will not be disgraced; for you will forget the shame of your youth, and the reproach of your widowhood you will remember no more.
i18n.he: אַל־תִּֽירְאִי֙ כִּי־לֹ֣א תֵב֔וֹשִׁי וְאַל־תִּכָּלְמִ֖י כִּ֣י לֹ֣א תַחְפִּ֑ירִי כִּ֣י בֹ֤שֶׁת עֲלוּמַ֙יִךְ֙ תִּשְׁכָּ֔חִי וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת אַלְמְנוּתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֥א תִזְכְּרִי־עֽוֹד׃

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י בֹעֲלַ֙יִךְ֙ עֹשַׂ֔יִךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ וְגֹֽאֲלֵךְ֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֱלֹהֵ֥י כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יִקָּרֵֽא׃

i18n.en: For your husband is your Maker — YHWH of hosts is his name — and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; he is called the God of the whole earth.
i18n.he: כִּ֤י בֹעֲלַ֙יִךְ֙ עֹשַׂ֔יִךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ וְגֹֽאֲלֵךְ֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֱלֹהֵ֥י כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יִקָּרֵֽא׃

notes.official: *kî ḇōʿălayiḵ ʿōśayiḵ* “For your husband is your Maker.” Both participles are formally plural (“your husbands, your makers”), the plural of majesty also found at Job 35:10 (*ʿōśāy*) and Ps 149:2 (*ʿōśāyw*). The line renders them singular with ASV, NRSV and NJPS, because the following “YHWH of hosts is his name” fixes a single referent, and records the plural form here. *ʿōśeh* is cited to the central `asah` entry. *ʾĕlōhê ḵol-hā-ʾāreṣ* “the God of the whole earth” follows the overlay construct-epithet pattern.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־כְאִשָּׁ֧ה עֲזוּבָ֛ה וַעֲצ֥וּבַת ר֖וּחַ קְרָאָ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֧שֶׁת נְעוּרִ֛ים כִּ֥י תִמָּאֵ֖ס אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃

i18n.en: For YHWH has called you like a wife forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth when she is cast off, says your God.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־כְאִשָּׁ֧ה עֲזוּבָ֛ה וַעֲצ֥וּבַת ר֖וּחַ קְרָאָ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֧שֶׁת נְעוּרִ֛ים כִּ֥י תִמָּאֵ֖ס אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃

paragraphs.text: בְּרֶ֥גַע קָטֹ֖ן עֲזַבְתִּ֑יךְ וּבְרַחֲמִ֥ים גְּדֹלִ֖ים אֲקַבְּצֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will gather you.
i18n.he: בְּרֶ֥גַע קָטֹ֖ן עֲזַבְתִּ֑יךְ וּבְרַחֲמִ֥ים גְּדֹלִ֖ים אֲקַבְּצֵֽךְ׃

notes.official:
*bᵉregaʿ qāṭōn ʿăzaḇtîḵ ûḇᵉraḥămîm gᵉḏōlîm ʾăqabbᵉṣēḵ* “For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will gather you.” *raḥămîm* “compassion” is the plural of *reḥem* “womb.” *qbṣ* “gather” is the verb of the ingathering of the dispersed (43:5).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 5) quotes v. 7 and reads it as the return of the Jewish people to their land in the modern era. In the Hebrew the verse is addressed to Zion as a forsaken wife taken back, and the line renders it so.

paragraphs.text: בְּשֶׁ֣צֶף קֶ֗צֶף הִסְתַּ֨רְתִּי פָנַ֥י רֶ֙גַע֙ מִמֵּ֔ךְ וּבְחֶ֥סֶד עוֹלָ֖ם רִֽחַמְתִּ֑יךְ אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: In a surge of wrath I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have compassion on you, says YHWH your Redeemer.
i18n.he: בְּשֶׁ֣צֶף קֶ֗צֶף הִסְתַּ֨רְתִּי פָנַ֥י רֶ֙גַע֙ מִמֵּ֔ךְ וּבְחֶ֥סֶד עוֹלָ֖ם רִֽחַמְתִּ֑יךְ אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official: *bᵉšeṣep̄ qeṣep̄* “in a surge of wrath” is a sound-play (*šeṣep̄* is a hapax, “flood, overflowing”). *ûḇᵉḥeseḏ ʿôlām* “with everlasting kindness” is rendered under the central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness` entry (“kindness”).

paragraphs.text: כִּי־מֵ֥י נֹ֙חַ֙ זֹ֣את לִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי מֵעֲבֹ֥ר מֵי־נֹ֛חַ ע֖וֹד עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֥ן נִשְׁבַּ֛עְתִּי מִקְּצֹ֥ף עָלַ֖יִךְ וּמִגְּעָר־בָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: For this is the waters of Noah to me: as I swore that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you, nor rebuke you.
i18n.he: כִּי־מֵ֥י נֹ֙חַ֙ זֹ֣את לִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי מֵעֲבֹ֥ר מֵי־נֹ֛חַ ע֖וֹד עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֥ן נִשְׁבַּ֛עְתִּי מִקְּצֹ֥ף עָלַ֖יִךְ וּמִגְּעָר־בָּֽךְ׃

notes.official: MT *kî-mê nōaḥ zōʾṯ lî* is “For this is the waters of Noah to me”; ASV supplies “as.” Many manuscripts, the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ, כימי) and the ancient versions read *kîmê nōaḥ* “like the days of Noah,” which most modern versions adopt. The line keeps MT under the translation’s textual policy. The oath recalls the covenant after the Flood (Gen 9:11–15).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י הֶֽהָרִים֙ יָמ֔וּשׁוּ וְהַגְּבָע֖וֹת תְּמוּטֶ֑נָה וְחַסְדִּ֞י מֵאִתֵּ֣ךְ לֹֽא־יָמ֗וּשׁ וּבְרִ֤ית שְׁלוֹמִי֙ לֹ֣א תָמ֔וּט אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For the mountains may depart and the hills be shaken, but my kindness shall not depart from you, and my covenant of peace shall not be shaken, says YHWH, who has compassion on you.
i18n.he: כִּ֤י הֶֽהָרִים֙ יָמ֔וּשׁוּ וְהַגְּבָע֖וֹת תְּמוּטֶ֑נָה וְחַסְדִּ֞י מֵאִתֵּ֣ךְ לֹֽא־יָמ֗וּשׁ וּבְרִ֤ית שְׁלוֹמִי֙ לֹ֣א תָמ֔וּט אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official: *wᵉḥasdî mēʾittēḵ lōʾ-yāmûš ûḇᵉrîṯ šᵉlômî lōʾ ṯāmûṭ* “but my kindness shall not depart from you, and my covenant of peace shall not be shaken.” *ḥeseḏ* is “kindness” (central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`), and *bᵉrîṯ šālôm* “covenant of peace” is cited to the central `brit-shalom-mishkan` entry (Num 25:12; Ezek 34:25; 37:26).

paragraphs.text: עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַרְבִּ֤יץ בַּפּוּךְ֙ אֲבָנַ֔יִךְ וִיסַדְתִּ֖יךְ בַּסַּפִּירִֽים׃

i18n.en: O afflicted one, storm-tossed, not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in antimony, and lay your foundations with sapphires.
i18n.he: עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַרְבִּ֤יץ בַּפּוּךְ֙ אֲבָנַ֔יִךְ וִיסַדְתִּ֖יךְ בַּסַּפִּירִֽים׃

notes.official: *hinnēh ʾānōḵî marbîṣ bap-pûḵ ʾăḇānayiḵ* “behold, I will set your stones in antimony.” *pûḵ* is antimony or kohl, the dark eye-paint of 2 Kgs 9:30, here the dark mortar or setting that makes the gems stand out (NRSV “antimony”; cf. 1 Chr 29:2 *ʾaḇnê-p̄ûḵ*). ASV’s “fair colors” is a guess (overlay `lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah`). *sappîrîm* “sapphires” is probably lapis lazuli. The precious stones of vv. 11–12 (*kaḏkōḏ* “rubies,” *ʾeqdāḥ* “carbuncles”) are given the ASV identifications, which are uncertain.

paragraphs.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י כַּֽדְכֹד֙ שִׁמְשֹׁתַ֔יִךְ וּשְׁעָרַ֖יִךְ לְאַבְנֵ֣י אֶקְדָּ֑ח וְכָל־גְּבוּלֵ֖ךְ לְאַבְנֵי־חֵֽפֶץ׃

i18n.en: And I will make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of carbuncles, and all your border of precious stones.
i18n.he: וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י כַּֽדְכֹד֙ שִׁמְשֹׁתַ֔יִךְ וּשְׁעָרַ֖יִךְ לְאַבְנֵ֣י אֶקְדָּ֑ח וְכָל־גְּבוּלֵ֖ךְ לְאַבְנֵי־חֵֽפֶץ׃

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־בָּנַ֖יִךְ לִמּוּדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְרַ֖ב שְׁל֥וֹם בָּנָֽיִךְ׃

i18n.en: And all your children shall be taught by YHWH, and great shall be the peace of your children.
i18n.he: וְכָל־בָּנַ֖יִךְ לִמּוּדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְרַ֖ב שְׁל֥וֹם בָּנָֽיִךְ׃

notes.official: *wᵉḵol-bānayiḵ limmûḏê YHWH wᵉraḇ šᵉlôm bānāyiḵ* “And all your children shall be taught by YHWH, and great shall be the peace of your children.” The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) writes the second word with an extra *waw*, בוניכי *bônayiḵ* “your builders,” and the rabbis already played on the same pair: “do not read *bānayiḵ*, your children, but *bônayiḵ*, your builders” (b. Ber. 64a). The line keeps MT “your children” both times (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). John 6:45 quotes the first half.

paragraphs.text: בִּצְדָקָ֖ה תִּכּוֹנָ֑נִי רַחֲקִ֤י מֵעֹ֙שֶׁק֙ כִּֽי־לֹ֣א תִירָ֔אִי וּמִ֨מְּחִתָּ֔ה כִּ֥י לֹֽא־תִקְרַ֖ב אֵלָֽיִךְ׃

i18n.en: In righteousness you shall be established; you shall be far from oppression, for you shall not fear, and from terror, for it shall not come near you.
i18n.he: בִּצְדָקָ֖ה תִּכּוֹנָ֑נִי רַחֲקִ֤י מֵעֹ֙שֶׁק֙ כִּֽי־לֹ֣א תִירָ֔אִי וּמִ֨מְּחִתָּ֔ה כִּ֥י לֹֽא־תִקְרַ֖ב אֵלָֽיִךְ׃

paragraphs.text: הֵ֣ן גּ֥וֹר יָג֛וּר אֶ֖פֶס מֵֽאוֹתִ֑י מִי־גָ֥ר אִתָּ֖ךְ עָלַ֥יִךְ יִפּֽוֹל׃

i18n.en: Behold, they may gather together, but not by me; whoever gathers together against you shall fall because of you.
i18n.he: הֵ֣ן גּ֥וֹר יָג֛וּר אֶ֖פֶס מֵֽאוֹתִ֑י מִי־גָ֥ר אִתָּ֖ךְ עָלַ֥יִךְ יִפּֽוֹל׃

notes.official: *hēn gôr yāḡûr ʾep̄es mēʾôṯî* is “Behold, they may gather together, but not by me” (ASV). The verb *gwr* has three homonyms: “sojourn,” “gather, band together,” and “stir up strife, attack.” NRSV takes the third (“If anyone stirs up strife, it is not from me”). The line keeps ASV.

paragraphs.text: הן [הִנֵּ֤ה] אָֽנֹכִי֙ בָּרָ֣אתִי חָרָ֔שׁ נֹפֵ֙חַ֙ בְּאֵ֣שׁ פֶּחָ֔ם וּמוֹצִ֥יא כְלִ֖י לְמַעֲשֵׂ֑הוּ וְאָנֹכִ֛י בָּרָ֥אתִי מַשְׁחִ֖ית לְחַבֵּֽל׃

i18n.en: Behold, I have created the smith who blows the fire of coals and brings out a weapon for his work; and I have created the destroyer to ruin.
i18n.he: הן [הִנֵּ֤ה] אָֽנֹכִי֙ בָּרָ֣אתִי חָרָ֔שׁ נֹפֵ֙חַ֙ בְּאֵ֣שׁ פֶּחָ֔ם וּמוֹצִ֥יא כְלִ֖י לְמַעֲשֵׂ֑הוּ וְאָנֹכִ֛י בָּרָ֥אתִי מַשְׁחִ֖ית לְחַבֵּֽל׃

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere. The consonantal הן *hēn* is read הִנֵּה *hinnēh*, both “behold,” with no change of sense (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *ʾānōḵî bārāʾṯî ḥārāš … wᵉʾānōḵî bārāʾṯî mašḥîṯ lᵉḥabbēl* “I have created the smith … and I have created the destroyer to ruin.” YHWH made both the weapon-maker and the one who wields destruction, so no weapon can succeed without his consent (v. 17). *bārāʾ* is “create” (overlay `bara-create-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: כָּל־כְּלִ֞י יוּצַ֤ר עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ לֹ֣א יִצְלָ֔ח וְכָל־לָשׁ֛וֹן תָּֽקוּם־אִתָּ֥ךְ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט תַּרְשִׁ֑יעִי זֹ֡את נַחֲלַת֩ עַבְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה וְצִדְקָתָ֛ם מֵאִתִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper, and every tongue that rises against you in judgment you shall condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of YHWH, and their righteousness from me, says YHWH.
i18n.he: כָּל־כְּלִ֞י יוּצַ֤ר עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ לֹ֣א יִצְלָ֔ח וְכָל־לָשׁ֛וֹן תָּֽקוּם־אִתָּ֥ךְ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט תַּרְשִׁ֑יעִי זֹ֡את נַחֲלַת֩ עַבְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה וְצִדְקָתָ֛ם מֵאִתִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official: *kol-kᵉlî yûṣar ʿālayiḵ lōʾ yiṣlāḥ* “No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper.” *yûṣar* is the Hophal of *yāṣar* “form” (central `yatsar`), used of the smith’s work from v. 16. *ʿaḇdê YHWH* “the servants of YHWH”: from here on the book speaks of the servants in the plural (65:8–15).
